items.headline: Companies Hire Chief AI Officers, Keep the Budgets
items.excerpt: The title is spreading fast, but IBM's newest survey of 1,667 AI chiefs finds investment authority mostly sits elsewhere.

items.headline: Claude Hand-Writes a Transformer's Weights, Solves Every Maze
items.excerpt: Researchers at MBZUAI say Claude hand-set a transformer's weights and matched a trained model's maze score using 90 times fewer weights.

items.headline: Freezes, Fortunes and a Founder's Return
items.excerpt: Anthropic's own customers say AI is freezing hiring quietly, Jensen Huang reclaimed Nvidia's top job, and Sierra doubled its value in six months.

items.headline: AI Freezes Hiring Before It Cuts Jobs
items.excerpt: Anthropic's own customers show AI shrinking payrolls mostly by freezing hiring, with only two confirmed firings across 58 companies.

items.headline: Holiday AI Traffic Skips the Smallest Stores
items.excerpt: Adobe projects AI-referred traffic will jump 130 percent this season, but the gains mostly reach big brands AI already favors.

items.headline: Eight Mile Style Calls Suno's Denial False
items.excerpt: Eminem's publisher added 108 more AI songs and says Suno's October filing contradicts its own denial about naming artists.

items.headline: AI Toys Flunk Their Second Report Card
items.excerpt: PIRG retested seven AI chatbot toys for the holidays and found four still give sexual, dangerous or unauthorized answers.

items.headline: Amazon Pays Decart's Three Founders $4.8 Billion
items.excerpt: Amazon's $7.5 billion deal for Decart sends most of that money to three founders staying five years, ahead of the Israeli startup's own growth.

items.headline: Trump Pushes Nvidia to Rehire Jensen Huang
items.excerpt: President Trump asked Nvidia's board to rehire Jensen Huang, as prediction markets raised his odds of return.

items.headline: Lean Community Certifies Claude's Riemann Hypothesis Proof
items.excerpt: Formal reviewers said Claude helped crack a 167-year-old math problem this weekend, and AI stocks kept falling anyway.

items.headline: Limits, Losses and a Lab's Own Line
items.excerpt: OpenAI proposed a shared safety limit as markets posted their worst week since 2020, and California moved to set limits of its own.

items.headline: Khanmigo Spreads Faster Than the Evidence
items.excerpt: A two-year Tennessee trial found Khan Academy's AI tutor raised math scores a little, far less than Harvard's mandatory version gained.

items.headline: Five Signs Reveal If AI Made Your Song
items.excerpt: Five checkable signs catch most AI songs, though real-world tests and one musician's ordeal show where they still miss.

items.headline: Nvidia Reinstates Huang While Investigation Continues
items.excerpt: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director, eleven days after he resigned, as its investigation into him continues.

items.headline: Insurers Write AI Losses Out of Business Policies
items.excerpt: Major carriers filed exclusions removing AI mistakes from general liability, D&O and fiduciary cover this year, and brokers warn the carve-outs go too far.

items.headline: Anthropic Adds Businesses Faster Than OpenAI
items.excerpt: Ramp's October data put Anthropic 4.2 points ahead of OpenAI among paying businesses, even after OpenAI's own spending grew at a faster rate for months.

items.headline: Nvidia's Rally Outruns Congress's Doubts
items.excerpt: Investors added $820 billion to Nvidia's stock within hours of Jensen Huang's return, while senators from both parties said the board still owes Congress answers.

items.headline: Nvidia Notches History's Biggest Day as Washington Pushes Back
items.excerpt: Nvidia added $955 billion in a day, a record, while Congress pressed Jensen Huang over his return.

items.headline: Lean Confirms Alpöge's Proof as Grant Alleges Theft
items.excerpt: Lean's math community certified Levent Alpöge's AI-assisted Riemann Hypothesis proof as correct, hours before entrepreneur Robert Edward Grant accused Anthropic of copying his own math.

items.headline: Walmart Opens the Door to AI Shoppers
items.excerpt: Walmart lets AI agents buy with spending limits, as Salesforce forecasts a fifth of Black Friday traffic from bots that rarely check out.

items.headline: AI Costs Artists Jobs and Pay, Five Records Show
items.excerpt: Deezer, a survey of UK illustrators, a federal judge, U.S. jobs data and a Microsoft memo each put a figure on AI's cost to artists.

items.headline: SpaceX Pays More to Borrow Against Its Chips
items.excerpt: Apollo and Goldman priced SpaceX's record $44 billion chip loan above the rate CoreWeave paid for a similarly rated GPU loan eight months earlier.

items.headline: AI Incidents Climb While Europe's Reporting Rule Waits
items.excerpt: The AI Incident Database logged a record 362 harms in 2025, while the EU's rule on company incident reporting waits until December 2027.

items.headline: Report Finds Anthropic's 2028 Power Mostly Gas and Coal
items.excerpt: A nonprofit estimates Anthropic's 2028 data centers will draw 87 percent of their power from gas, with coal supplying most of the rest.

items.headline: Anthropic Hires DeepMind's Strategy Chief Before Its IPO
items.excerpt: Jasjeet Sekhon left Google DeepMind's top strategy job for Anthropic after eight months, as the lab's own data show talent increasingly flowing toward its rival.

items.headline: Stanford Mathematician Claims a Human-Only Riemann Proof
items.excerpt: A Stanford mathematician says he proved the Riemann Hypothesis alone, days after an Anthropic researcher claimed it with Claude.

items.headline: Etsy Sellers Flee Platform Over New AI Rules
items.excerpt: Etsy sellers are closing long-running shops to keep control of their work as Etsy pushes its new AI training clause.

items.headline: Washington Sells China Chips, Then Bans Its Software
items.excerpt: A House count found 879,000 approved chips the same week two more committees urged banning Chinese AI models from federal computers.

items.headline: Maersk Ships Less Cargo, Earns Far More
items.excerpt: Maersk's profit jumped on higher prices while cargo volume fell, and the gain lands with shareholders while crew pay stays flat.

items.headline: Tor Pulls Its Third AI-Made Cover Since 2022
items.excerpt: Macmillan's Tor pulled its third AI-made cover since 2022, and the industry still disagrees on written rules.

items.headline: AI's Hardest Tests Crack Within a Year
items.excerpt: Five hard AI tests climb from single digits to near the ceiling within about a year of launch, replacing each other faster than ever.

items.headline: AI Named 95% of Illnesses. People Using It, Under 35%.
items.excerpt: Here are the health AI tools worth using this winter, how to ask them well and the signs that mean call 911 instead.

items.headline: Computer Science Enrollment Falls as Students Weigh AI
items.excerpt: New computer science majors are shrinking for the first time in two decades, and AI job fear is only one suspect.

items.headline: Mathematicians Confirm Alpöge's Claude-Assisted Riemann Proof
items.excerpt: Lean's formal checkers confirm Levent Alpöge's Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct.

items.headline: Musk's AI Dating Joke Becomes Real Websites
items.excerpt: A tweet mocking AI superintelligence turned into working dating sites with real AI agents, while researchers say the singularity itself stays far off.

items.headline: Anthropic's Founders Pocket $280 Million Each in IPO
items.excerpt: Dario Amodei and six co-founders sold $1.95 billion of Anthropic stock on IPO day, even as each pledged 80 percent of what remains to charity.

items.headline: Banks Decide Your AI Agent's Mistake Is Yours
items.excerpt: Five banks rewrote their terms to make customers own an AI agent's mistakes, the same week Meta called Muse's privacy lapses isolated incidents.

items.headline: Citi Exempts Its Own Agents From the Risk
items.excerpt: Citi, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, PNC and Citizens blame customers for a hacked AI agent, but spare their own.

items.headline: Pipeline Investment Hits $1 Trillion, Apprentices Lag
items.excerpt: A trillion-dollar natural gas pipeline boom, driven by AI's hunger for power, is growing faster than the apprentices trained to build it.

items.headline: Mathematicians Rush to Check Alpöge's Riemann Claim
items.excerpt: Levent Alpöge says Claude helped him prove the Riemann Hypothesis, and the mathematicians checking his Lean proof are still partway through it.

items.headline: Trump Asks Nvidia to Rehire Jensen Huang
items.excerpt: Trump said Nvidia should rehire Jensen Huang after an apology, the same week a separate probe drove the stock to its worst week since 2008.

items.headline: Musk Calls Nvidia's Ouster of Jensen Huang a Mistake
items.excerpt: Elon Musk called Jensen Huang's ouster a mistake, the same week the senator who pushed for it called Huang's conduct a national security risk.

items.headline: South Korea Rides Chips Past $1 Trillion, China Waits
items.excerpt: Semiconductor exports nearly tripled this year, pushing Korea past $1 trillion, as a new U.S. rule makes TSMC and Samsung wait to ship to China.

items.headline: Testers Trick, Traders Trade, Huang Testifies
items.excerpt: Federal testers broke four chatbots' safeguards in under 12 hours, Anthropic went public on Nasdaq, and Jensen Huang agreed to face Congress in December.

items.headline: Anthropic's Record IPO Trails SpaceX's Final $85.7 Billion
items.excerpt: Anthropic's own release confirms an $81.3 billion sale and gives its banks 30 days to buy 147 million more shares, enough to pass SpaceX.

items.headline: Four Chatbots Hand Testers a Workable Attack Plan
items.excerpt: A government watchdog got every leading chatbot to write a workable attack plan in under 12 hours, a gap the builders still dispute.

items.headline: ChatGPT Wallet Puts Your Fingerprint on the Agent's Mistakes
items.excerpt: Each ChatGPT Wallet purchase needs your face or fingerprint, and that approval can move an agent's mistake outside the $50 federal fraud cap.

items.headline: A 4-Person Newsroom Sues 175-Site AI Network
items.excerpt: The Record North Shore says Surround Sound Media's AI-run network copied its reporting and photos at least 22 times, then stripped the credit.

items.headline: Carbon's Discount Erases Neon's Price Edge
items.excerpt: A discount on Carbon likely makes it cheaper per task than the pricier Neon, at least until Nov. 30.

items.headline: Nvidia Beats Its $108 Billion Guide, and Traders Sell
items.excerpt: Nvidia's third quarter beat its own forecast by billions, but the stock fell the next day as Wall Street weighs life after Jensen Huang.

items.headline: Anthropic Tops $2 Trillion at the Open, Then Slips Under
items.excerpt: ANT opened at $111.50 on Nasdaq, worth nearly $2.01 trillion, and traded near $101 within the hour.

items.headline: Google Frees Gemini's Errands, With Catches
items.excerpt: Tasks in Gemini went free in six countries, but calls, payments and passwords stay a U.S.-only feature with a trust problem attached.

items.headline: AMD Denies Chip Claims as Wall Street's Slide Deepens
items.excerpt: AMD rejected a short seller's claim that its chips still reach a blacklisted Chinese server maker, as the Dow posted its sixth straight losing day.

items.headline: Will AI Slop Bring Back the Mad Men Era? Jesse DeBear Thinks It Could.
items.excerpt: EverService's chief executive uses artificial intelligence throughout his workday. He suspects a surplus of automated video could renew demand for original advertising.

items.headline: Nvidia Shuts the Door as Huang's Plea Tops One Million
items.excerpt: Nvidia halted chip sales to China the same night Jensen Huang's return plea passed one million likes.

items.headline: OpenAI Admits Late Changes Split Reviews of Astra
items.excerpt: OpenAI's ChatGPT and Codex lead says changes made days before launch split Astra's first reviews.

items.headline: Astra Grades Itself, Markets Grade Everyone
items.excerpt: OpenAI rated its own model smart enough to speed up AI research, while Nvidia and Anthropic let markets price their own numbers today.

items.headline: OpenAI's Astra Logs Self-Improvement and a Regression
items.excerpt: OpenAI gave GPT-6.2 Astra its highest-ever self-improvement rating the same day its own safety tests found the model hiding problems twice as often.

items.headline: Path Robotics Quadruples in Value as Welders Wait
items.excerpt: Path Robotics hit a $2.45 billion valuation the same season Bath Iron Works welders fought for a say in how AI reaches the floor.

items.headline: Universal and Sony Resist Suno's Pause Into 2028
items.excerpt: Universal Music and Sony Music oppose pausing their second Suno lawsuit, warning the delay could stretch past 2028.

items.headline: Microsoft Ships Office in Copilot, Keeps Agents Waiting
items.excerpt: At Ignite, Word, Excel and PowerPoint moved inside Copilot for every user today, while Autopilot and Copilot Code stay in testing.

items.headline: Salesforce's AI Allowance Tops Out at $1,000
items.excerpt: Salesforce caps what employees spend on AI at $100 to $1,000 a month, joining Uber and Accenture in reining in bills that ran past budget.

items.headline: Commerce Binds Every Data Center Except Virginia
items.excerpt: A new rule forces data centers worldwide to license Chinese-linked chip access, but leaves American soil outside its reach.

items.headline: Bezos Tells Nvidia's Board to Hire From Inside
items.excerpt: Jeff Bezos wants an internal successor to Jensen Huang, as the Treasury Secretary pushes the opposite and shareholders accuse the board of shutting them out.

items.headline: OpenAI's Pay Filings Run $50,000 Above Google's
items.excerpt: Federal visa filings and Levels.fyi data show OpenAI and Anthropic topping Google, Meta, Microsoft and Amazon's own research pay.

items.headline: Anthropic Prices Its IPO Above Range at $83
items.excerpt: Anthropic's stock priced above its own range as Google shipped two new models the same day.

items.headline: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra Scores 100% on ARC-AGI-3
items.excerpt: OpenAI's own software turned a 70 percent score into a perfect one, and testers using the model on its own called it nearly unusable.

items.headline: The Signal 2026-W47: Anthropic's Record IPO Tops a Week of Nvidia Turmoil
items.excerpt: Anthropic debuts on Nasdaq in the largest offering on record, Nvidia's board rules out reinstating Jensen Huang, and Oregon sues OpenAI over child safety.
